newsitem.title: USA: Ex-White House aide denies seeking immunity deal.
newsitem.headline: Ex-White House aide denies seeking immunity deal.

text.p: Former White House aide Mark Middleton denied on Tuesday seeking immunity from prosecution for his cooperation with investigators probing the money trail into the United States from Indonesia's Lippo Group.

The Washington Post reported that Middleton, a former top aide to then-Chief of Staff Mack McLarty, had offered to give narrow testimony in the Whitewater investigation in exchange for immunity from prosecution.
"I have engaged in no conduct that would require immunity and there is no deal. The story is categorically false and destructive," Middleton said in a statement.
Middleton, an Arkansas native, left the government in February 1995 to work as an international consultant in Indonesia and other parts of Asia.
The Post, quoting unnamed sources, said Middleton had offered to testify about a dinner that he attended with former Associate Attorney General Webster Hubbell shortly after he left the White House.

Whitewater independent counsel Kenneth Starr is investigating payments Hubbell received totalling nearly $500,000 for work he did after leaving government to find out if the work was orchestrated by the White House in exchange for his silence on Whitewater matters.
One Hubbell payment for $100,000 came in June 1994 from Lippo.
"I personally played absolutely no role in arranging payments to Mr. Hubbell and did not directly or indirectly facilitate such payments," Middleton said.

"I am not aware of any information to suggest that the payments made or arranged by others were motivated by any improper purpose," he said. "I am not aware of any information regarding the Lippo Group that would be of interest to prosecutors."

"Further, as I have stressed many times, I have not personally engaged in any illegal or improper conduct in any matter of interest to the independent counsel, the Justice Department or Congress," Middleton said.
The Justice Department and congressional committees are investigating whether individuals with ties to Lippo engaged in illegal campaign fund-raising activities involving last year's election.

McLarty and others close to the Clintons initiated the effort to find work for Hubbell. Starr's prosecutors last week called McLarty before a federal grand jury in Little Rock to question him about the efforts to find work for Hubbell.
